# Multi-Stage Dockerfile for Node.js TypeScript Application

## Project Structure
```
project/
├── Dockerfile
├── .dockerignore
├── package.json
├── package-lock.json
├── tsconfig.json
└── src/
    └── index.ts
```

## Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# ============================================================
# Stage 1: Dependencies
# Install ALL dependencies (including devDependencies)
# ============================================================
FROM node:20-alpine AS dependencies

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker layer caching
# Layers are only rebuilt when these files change
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./

# Install all dependencies including devDependencies needed for TypeScript compilation
# --frozen-lockfile ensures reproducible builds
RUN npm ci --frozen-lockfile

# ============================================================
# Stage 2: Builder
# Compile TypeScript to JavaScript
# ============================================================
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# Copy installed node_modules from dependencies stage
COPY --from=dependencies /app/node_modules ./node_modules

# Copy TypeScript configuration and source files
COPY tsconfig.json ./
COPY src/ ./src/

# Copy package.json (needed for npm scripts)
COPY package.json ./

# Compile TypeScript → JavaScript
# Output goes to /app/dist (as configured in tsconfig.json)
RUN npm run build

# ============================================================
# Stage 3: Production Dependencies
# Install ONLY production dependencies for the final image
# ============================================================
FROM node:20-alpine AS prod-dependencies

WORKDIR /app

COPY package.json package-lock.json ./

# Install only production dependencies, skip devDependencies
# This significantly reduces node_modules size
RUN npm ci --frozen-lockfile --omit=dev

# ============================================================
# Stage 4: Final / Runtime Image
# Minimal image with only what's needed to run the app
# ============================================================
FROM node:20-alpine AS final

# Install dumb-init for proper signal handling and PID 1 management
# This ensures graceful shutdowns work correctly in containers
RUN apk add --no-cache dumb-init

# Create a non-root user for security
# Running as root inside containers is a security risk
RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs && \
    adduser  --system --uid 1001 --ingroup nodejs nodeuser

WORKDIR /app

# Copy only production node_modules from prod-dependencies stage
COPY --from=prod-dependencies /app/node_modules ./node_modules

# Copy compiled JavaScript from builder stage
# We do NOT copy TypeScript source or tsconfig into the final image
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist

# Copy package.json (needed for Node.js module resolution)
COPY package.json ./

# Set ownership of all files to the non-root user
RUN chown -R nodeuser:nodejs /app

# Switch to non-root user
USER nodeuser

# Document the port the application listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Set NODE_ENV to production
# This affects many libraries' behavior (e.g., Express disables verbose errors)
ENV NODE_ENV=production

# Use dumb-init as the entrypoint to handle signals properly
# Then run the compiled JavaScript entry point
ENTRYPOINT ["dumb-init", "--"]
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
```

## .dockerignore

```dockerignore
# Version control
.git
.gitignore

# Node modules (will be installed fresh in Docker)
node_modules

# TypeScript source (not needed in final image)
src/

# Build output (will be compiled in Docker)
dist/

# Development and config files
.env
.env.*
*.env
.eslintrc*
.prettierrc*
jest.config*
*.test.ts
*.spec.ts
__tests__/

# Documentation
README.md
docs/

# Docker files themselves
Dockerfile
.dockerignore

# OS artifacts
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db

# IDE files
.vscode/
.idea/
*.swp
*.swo

# Logs
logs/
*.log
npm-debug.log*

# Coverage reports
coverage/
```

## Supporting Files

### tsconfig.json
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "commonjs",
    "lib": ["ES2022"],
    "outDir": "./dist",
    "rootDir": "./src",
    "strict": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "declarationMap": false,
    "sourceMap": false
  },
  "include": ["src/**/*"],
  "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "**/*.test.ts", "**/*.spec.ts"]
}
```

### package.json
```json
{
  "name": "my-ts-app",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Node.js TypeScript application",
  "main": "dist/index.js",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "tsc --project tsconfig.json",
    "start": "node dist/index.js",
    "dev": "ts-node src/index.ts",
    "lint": "eslint src/**/*.ts",
    "test": "jest"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "express": "^4.18.2"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/express": "^4.17.21",
    "@types/node": "^20.10.0",
    "typescript": "^5.3.2"
  }
}
```

### src/index.ts
```typescript
import express, { Request, Response } from 'express';

const app = express();
const PORT = process.env.PORT ?? 3000;

app.use(express.json());

app.get('/health', (_req: Request, res: Response) => {
  res.json({
    status: 'healthy',
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    environment: process.env.NODE_ENV,
  });
});

app.get('/', (_req: Request, res: Response) => {
  res.json({ message: 'Hello from TypeScript + Docker!' });
});

app.listen(PORT, () => {
  console.log(`Server running on port ${PORT} in ${process.env.NODE_ENV} mode`);
});
```

## Build & Run Commands

```bash
# Build the image
docker build -t my-ts-app:latest .

# Build with a specific target stage (useful for debugging)
docker build --target builder -t my-ts-app:debug .

# Run the container
docker run -p 3000:3000 --env NODE_ENV=production my-ts-app:latest

# Run with environment file
docker run -p 3000:3000 --env-file .env my-ts-app:latest

# Check the final image size
docker image inspect my-ts-app:latest --format='{{.Size}}' | \
  awk '{printf "%.2f MB\n", $1/1024/1024}'

# Compare sizes across stages
docker images | grep my-ts-app
```

## How Each Stage Reduces Image Size

```
┌─────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Stage               │ Purpose & What Gets Discarded                    │
├─────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ dependencies        │ Installs ALL deps → discarded entirely           │
│ builder             │ Compiles TS → .ts files, tsconfig discarded      │
│ prod-dependencies   │ Only prod deps → devDependencies discarded       │
│ final               │ Only dist/ + prod node_modules → ~80MB total     │
└─────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Typical size comparison:
  Single-stage (naive):  ~1.2 GB
  Multi-stage (this):    ~180 MB
  Savings:               ~85%
```

## Key Design Decisions

| Decision | Reason |
|---|---|
| `node:20-alpine` base | Alpine Linux is ~5MB vs ~900MB for full Debian |
| Separate `prod-dependencies` stage | Avoids devDependencies in final image |
| `dumb-init` | Proper PID 1 signal handling, prevents zombie processes |
| Non-root user | Security best practice; limits blast radius of exploits |
| `sourceMap: false` in tsconfig | Excludes source maps from dist/, reducing size |
| `COPY package.json` before source | Maximizes Docker layer cache hits |
| `npm ci` over `npm install` | Reproducible, faster, respects lockfile exactly |
